Anita (Product): Quick sync — we need a final decision set for the Operator bundle release next week. Main tradeoffs to close out: bundle size vs offline-installer ergonomics, customer KMS/HSM support vs rollout friction, preserve customer egress IP vs simpler networking, and upgrade path (zero-downtime) vs safe rollback. Short replies plz.

Diego (Eng): I can outline technical constraints quickly. Slim operator (no embedded large images, relies on external image registry) saves ~600MB and speeds installs on constrained hosts, but customers doing airgap will want a tarball they can import. Supporting both is doable but increases test matrix.

Priya (Field): FYI — three pilot customers called this morning: one absolutely requires offline tarball + clear install checklist, another insists on egress IP preservation for allowlisting, third is okay with registry pulls if we provide presigned images. So offline installer + IP preserve are high on field asks.

Sam W. (Eng Runtime): Upgrade note: to get near-zero downtime we need: rolling operator upgrade + preflight CRD validation + KV cache drain/rehydration step. That adds ~1–2 hours to rollout windows depending on model cache sizes. If we pick simpler rollback-first approach we can reduce rollout complexity.

Maya (Security): KMS guidance: we should support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) as a priority, and HSM integration as an opt-in enterprise add-on. HSM/HSM-backed tokens add a lot of operational burden for installs. Can we gate HSM behind enterprise checkbox?

Diego (Eng): Suggested ship option matrix:
- Option A: Slim operator + offline tarball artifact + documented rollback (target: GA).
- Option B: Full bundle (images included) + KMS & IP-preservation enabled by default (target: GA, higher risk/time).
- Option C: Phased GA: A now, B in v1.1.

Priya (Field): Field recommendation = Option A then v1.1 to add B features. Many customers can tolerate v1.1 timeline if A has robust docs and a clean rollback.

Anita (Product): Quick technical ask: how heavy is the preflight webhook for A? can it run as a fast check so installs don't stall?

Sam W. (Eng Runtime): Preflight can be lightweight: check CRDs, node selectors, available GPU-reqs, and basic connectivity. Example quick check:
```bash
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep Ready
kubectl -n redwood get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.phase}'
```
Deeper checks (KMS endpoints, IP assignment tests) would be optional steps for the full bundle.

Maya (Security): Also add a short KMS threat checklist to the installer flow so customers know which perms are needed.

Diego (Eng): Rollback plan for A: operator supports "pause" annotation + previous CRD version restore. We should include a one-command rollback in docs. Implementation effort ~2 dev-weeks + QA.

Priya (Field): Documentation ask: network diagrams for three topologies — NATed egress, preserved-eip, and on-prem with direct peering. Also a checklist for firewall rules.

Anita (Product): OK decision proposal: Ship Option A as GA (slim operator + offline tarball + documented one-command rollback + lightweight preflight). Queue IP-preservation and default KMS integration for v1.1. If you agree, react here: :+1: for Option A now, :thumbsdown: to delay and push for full bundle GA.

Diego (Eng): :+1:
Sam W. (Eng Runtime): :+1:
Priya (Field): :+1:
Maya (Security): :+1: (with HSM gated to enterprise later)

deploy-bot: Created task RDW-1428 for "Operator bundle: implement offline tarball and rollback docs" and linked RDW-1430 for preflight checks.

Anita (Product): Thanks — I'll update the release plan and ping legal/solutions for the v1.1 commitment timeline. If any objections, flag in-thread before EOD.
